_note: DECLARED term mappings for RFQ-18649 group and assessment-area columns. There is no fuzzy matching anywhere in this package: a term absent from this file is reported UNMAPPED, never guessed into the nearest bucket. Every entry carries a kind so a reviewer can accept the mechanical ones and argue only the judgments.

kinds.EXACT_VARIANT: Same words, different case, spacing or separator. Mechanical; safe to accept.
kinds.DECLARED_JUDGMENT: Different words, judged equivalent by this package. A reviewer may disagree; the original term is always retained.
kinds.SCOPE_VALUE: A legitimate value that is not one of the three groups - it describes scope, not a mis-spelling.
kinds.GRANULARITY_MISMATCH: The term is finer-grained than the canonical. Mapped to its parent, but rows are NOT interchangeable with parent rows.
kinds.COMPOUND: One cell naming several areas at once. Parts are recorded; the cell is NOT split into independent rows.
kinds.AMBIGUOUS: Could serve more than one canonical term. Deliberately not mapped.
kinds.UNRESOLVED_CONCEPT: Names a concept this package will not equate with any canonical term. Needs the owning lane to decide.

group.CROSS_GROUP: Applies across groups rather than to one

deployment.basis: the shorter term is read as the deployment half of deployment/operations; a lane using it may or may not intend operations as well
deployment.question: Does 'deployment' in this lane cover operations, or only release execution?

software_delivery.basis: read as the same area the RFQ calls software development; 'delivery' and 'development' are not identical words and a lane may mean a narrower thing
software_delivery.question: Does 'software_delivery' cover development practice, or only the release pipeline?

software.basis: both software_development and software_delivery exist elsewhere in the tree; the bare term cannot be assigned to either without asking
software.question: Is 'software' here software_development or software_delivery?

operational_reliability.basis: reliability of a service in operation is an OUTCOME; deployment and operations is a PRACTICE area. Equating them would fabricate agreement between two lanes that may be measuring different things.
operational_reliability.question: Is operational_reliability intended as the DEP practice area, or as an outcome measured across areas? Joining on it is unsafe until the owning lane answers.

ESS-SYN.basis: origin-qualified spelling of the same fictional group; declared explicitly because same-looking values from different origins must not join by resemblance
ESS-SYN.question: Confirm ESS-SYN denotes the same fictional group as ESS.

ESS-FICTIONAL.basis: origin-qualified spelling of the same fictional group
ESS-FICTIONAL.question: Confirm ESS-FICTIONAL denotes the same fictional group as ESS.

RIS-FICTIONAL.question: Confirm RIS-FICTIONAL denotes the same fictional group as RIS.

IAM-FICTIONAL.question: Confirm IAM-FICTIONAL denotes the same fictional group as IAM.

CROSS.basis: names a cross-group scope; not a mis-spelling of a group

AIS.basis: the parent organisation containing all three groups; not itself one of them

iam-directory.basis: a service inside the IAM group; rows about one service are not interchangeable with rows about the group

iam-sso.basis: a service inside the IAM group; rows about one service are not interchangeable with rows about the group

iam-group-service.basis: a service inside the IAM group; rows about one service are not interchangeable with rows about the group

synthetic-registration.basis: a fictional service name with no declared parent group in the tree
synthetic-registration.question: Which of ESS/RIS/IAM owns the fictional 'synthetic-registration' service?
